headline: Google Keep lets you take notes without typing a single word
summary: Record voice memos, sketch ideas, or snap photos of handwritten notes. Google Keep transcribes and digitizes your input, making it easily searchable and editable.
details: Google Keep offers a surprisingly easy way to capture thoughts and information without ever touching the keyboard. Whether you're on the go or simply find typing tedious, Keep provides alternative methods to get your ideas down.

One of the most convenient features is voice recording. Simply open Keep, tap the plus button, and select 'Recording.' After you're done speaking, Keep saves the audio and automatically transcribes what you said, allowing you to read and edit the text directly.

This transcription feature is a game-changer for reminders, shopping lists, or article ideas. Instead of typing out multiple items, you can speak them aloud, let Keep transcribe the list, and then refine it into a checklist.

For visual thinkers, Keep's drawing feature allows you to sketch, doodle, or write with a finger or stylus. You can use various pen options and colors to create diagrams or jot down handwritten reminders, getting ideas out of your head and onto the screen.

Keep also integrates seamlessly with your camera. You can photograph handwritten notes from a notebook or whiteboard and save them directly to a note. This preserves the original information without the need for manual transcription.

Furthermore, Keep's 'Grab image text' option uses OCR (Optical Character Recognition) to extract readable words from images. This means you can photograph a page of text and then edit, copy, and reuse the extracted content within Keep, saving significant effort.

headline_marked: Grok releases [[first seven minutes]] of AI-generated 'Odyssey'
headline: Grok releases first seven minutes of AI-generated 'Odyssey'
summary: Elon Musk's AI venture Grok has published the initial segment of its 'Odyssey' series, aiming for historical accuracy.
details: Three months after Elon Musk announced Grok would create an AI-generated "Odyssey" movie, the company has released the first seven minutes, titled 'Episode 1 of our Odyssey series.'

Musk had previously criticized Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey' for its casting choices, contrasting it with Grok's approach. Nolan, a self-proclaimed 'techno-skeptic,' emphasized practical filmmaking for his successful adaptation.

The Grok version, a collaboration with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker, features characters with 'Musk-approved skin color' and a narrator with a British accent. While some shots appear realistic, the overall production is criticized for lacking artistry and human interest.

Reviewers found the AI-generated dialogue stilted and the pacing slow, making it difficult to maintain interest, especially when compared to the nearly three-hour runtime of Nolan's film. The lack of momentum and emotional connection leaves viewers disengaged.
Despite the initial release, the article suggests a lack of compelling content, making it hard to envision interest in a full-length movie generated by Grok.
